title: What you need to know about Child Support Arrears

content.rendered:
Child support arrears can create stress for both parents, but ignoring the situation often makes it more complicated.

Whether you have fallen behind on payments or are trying to address unpaid child support, understanding your rights and options can help you take the next appropriate step.

Falling behind on child support can be stressful for everyone involved. If you are the parent who is struggling to make payments, you may feel overwhelmed as the unpaid balance continues to grow. If you are the parent waiting for support, missed payments can create financial uncertainty and make it harder to cover your child’s everyday needs.

When child support payments are not made as ordered, the unpaid amount may be referred to as child support arrears.

Understanding what arrears are and what they may mean for your situation can help you decide what to do next.

What Are Child Support Arrears?

Child support arrears are unpaid child support amounts that have accumulated over time.

For example, if a parent is ordered to pay child support each month but misses one or more payments, the unpaid balance may continue to add up. Even if the parent’s financial circumstances have changed, an existing child support order generally remains in effect unless it is officially modified.

This means that simply being unable to make a payment does not automatically erase the obligation.

Why Child Support Arrears Can Add Up Quickly

A missed payment may not seem significant at first, but unpaid child support can accumulate over time.

This can become especially challenging when a parent experiences a job loss, reduction in income, or another unexpected financial change. Waiting too long to address the issue may allow the unpaid balance to continue growing.

If your financial circumstances have changed, understanding your options as early as possible may help you avoid additional complications.

What If You Cannot Keep Up With Your Payments?

If you are struggling to make your child support payments, it can be tempting to simply stop paying until your financial situation improves.

However, an existing court order does not automatically change because your income or circumstances have changed.

Depending on your situation, it may be possible to request a modification of the child support order. Taking action early can be important, especially if you know that your current financial situation may make it difficult to continue meeting your obligation.

What If You Are Owed Unpaid Child Support?

If you are not receiving the child support that has been ordered, the situation can be frustrating and financially difficult.

Keeping clear records of missed payments and any related communication can help you understand the amount that may be owed. Depending on the circumstances, there may also be options available to address the unpaid child support and enforce the existing order.

You do not necessarily have to simply accept ongoing missed payments.

Understanding Your Options

Child support arrears can create stress for both parents, but ignoring the situation often makes it more complicated.

Whether you have fallen behind on payments or are trying to address unpaid child support, understanding your rights and options can help you take the next appropriate step.

At The Drake Law Firm, we understand that child support issues can affect your finances, your family, and your peace of mind. Our team can help you review your situation, understand the options available to you, and determine the next steps based on your circumstances.
